lead.headline: US CBDC Ban and Circle's Charter Signal a Private-Sector Stablecoin Hegemony
lead.tldr: The simultaneous legislative block on a US CBDC and Circle's national trust bank charter effectively outsource the US digital dollar's infrastructure to private issuers.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, here is what moved in Web3 over the last 24 hours and why it matters for the quarter ahead.

top_signals.title: US CBDC Ban to Go into Effect without Trump Signoff on Housing Bill
top_signals.summary: A bipartisan US housing bill that includes a ban on the issuance of a digital dollar (CBDC) until 2030 is set to become law. The legislation will take effect even without President Trump's explicit signature due to a 10-day inaction period.
top_signals.why_it_matters: A statutory ban on a CBDC until 2030 removes the primary sovereign competitor to private stablecoins in the US market.

top_signals.title: USDC issuer Circle wins final approval for US national trust bank charter20m
top_signals.summary: Circle, the issuer of the USDC stablecoin, has received final approval for a US national trust bank charter. This regulatory milestone allows the company to operate as a federally chartered bank, enhancing its legitimacy and operational capabilities within the US financial system.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Circle's national trust bank charter bridges the gap between stablecoin issuance and federal banking legitimacy, reducing systemic regulatory risk.

top_signals.title: Circle wins licence for some US banking activities
top_signals.summary: Circle has been granted a license to operate as a trust bank, allowing it to engage in specific US banking activities. This regulatory approval is seen as a significant step for the stablecoin issuer's integration with traditional financial systems.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Direct access to US banking activities allows Circle to optimize its reserve management and payment rails without relying on third-party intermediaries.

top_signals.title: Kraken Plans AI-Powered Trading App Overhaul, CNBC Reports
top_signals.summary: Kraken is planning a comprehensive overhaul of its trading application to integrate AI-powered trading agents. This move reflects a broader trend of crypto exchanges and fintech firms adopting artificial intelligence to enhance digital finance services.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Kraken's shift toward AI agents suggests a move from passive trading interfaces to active, intent-based execution models.

top_signals.title: Here's what's next for the Clarity Act as Congress returns to Washington
top_signals.summary: The U.S. Congress is preparing to resume sessions in Washington to address cryptocurrency legislation, specifically the Clarity Act. This legislative push is expected to occur before the midterm election schedule begins.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The Clarity Act's progression will determine the specific compliance burdens for stablecoin issuers operating under the new banking charters.

deals.summary: TeraWulf is reportedly seeking a $3.5 billion debt raise to fund the development of a data center linked to AI firm Anthropic. This move signals a strategic pivot or expansion from pure Bitcoin mining into high-performance computing (HPC) and AI infrastructure.

on_the_radar.title: SK Hynix’s $26.5 billion US listing brought to Telegram users via xStocks
on_the_radar.summary: Tokenized shares of SK Hynix are now available to users on the Solana blockchain via platforms like Backpack, xStocks, and Ondo Finance. This integration allows Telegram users to access these assets through the xStocks interface.

on_the_radar.title: New Hampshire Council Votes Down $100M Bitcoin Bonds
on_the_radar.summary: The New Hampshire executive council rejected a proposal to issue $100 million in Bitcoin-backed bonds. The vote ended 3-2 against the Business Finance Authority's plan.

on_the_radar.title: Backpack joins race for 24/7 stock markets with tokenized equities21m
on_the_radar.summary: Backpack is entering the tokenized equities market to enable 24/7 trading of stocks. This move aims to merge traditional finance assets with the accessibility and efficiency of blockchain technology.

on_the_radar.title: Kraken to relaunch its mobile app with agentic trading and advise at the center
on_the_radar.summary: Kraken is relaunching its mobile application with a focus on agentic trading. The update will introduce autonomous AI agents capable of monitoring markets, suggesting trades, and executing them for users.

on_the_radar.title: Federal Reserve Taps A16z Co-Founder for Monetary Policy Task Force
on_the_radar.summary: The Federal Reserve has appointed a16z co-founder Marc Andreessen to lead a task force focused on the economic impact of emerging technologies. The initiative specifically aims to analyze how advancements like AI influence monetary policy.

on_the_radar.title: Binance co-CEO says 70% of EU withdrawals went to self-custody after MiCA deadline, with just 30% going to licensed platforms
on_the_radar.summary: Binance co-CEO Richard Teng reported that 70% of EU users who withdrew funds following the exchange's service suspension opted for self-custody. Only 30% of these withdrawals were directed toward other MiCA-licensed platforms.

on_the_radar.title: 'Communication challenge, nothing more': Standard Chartered keeps $100,000 bitcoin target, calls Strategy selloff a signaling problem
on_the_radar.summary: Standard Chartered maintains its price target of $100,000 for Bitcoin by the end of 2026. The bank views the recent selloff related to MicroStrategy's strategic pivot as a communication and signaling issue rather than a solvency crisis.

on_the_radar.title: Revolut integrates its crypto exchange with AI assistants as agentic trading spreads
on_the_radar.summary: Revolut has integrated its crypto exchange with several AI assistants, including Claude and Gemini. This allows users to analyze data, backtest strategies, and execute trades using agentic AI prompts.

linkedin_post:
The US government just effectively outsourced its digital currency strategy. By allowing a ban on a CBDC until 2030 to take effect while simultaneously granting Circle a national trust bank charter, the US is betting on private stablecoins to handle the plumbing of digital dollars. 

What I keep coming back to is the timing. Circle isn't just getting a license; they are becoming a federally chartered bank. This removes the 'bank-run' risk associated with third-party custodians and integrates USDC directly into the US financial system. When you pair this with the legislative block on a sovereign digital dollar, the path to USDC becoming the default settlement layer for US digital commerce is much clearer. I'd watch how this affects the competitive moat for other issuers who lack similar federal standing. The regulatory moat is now as important as the liquidity moat.
